text:
alex.k: running a long-run KV cache daily job and wanted to share a weird pattern I found. baseline config: Llama-2-70b, MQA off, rope 512 scaling, page_size=64KB, eviction_threshold=0.75

maria.s: curious — what peculiarity?

alex.k: memory grows slowly for first ~45min then spikes and stays ~20% higher. not a leak per-se, looks like fragmentation + delayed reuse of pages. attaching profiling snippet below.

shawn: can you paste the hot paths? kernel selection logs?

alex.k: sure. this is trimmed: 
```
[2026-02-22T14:12:07Z] kernel_picker: selected kernel=matmul_opt_v3 for seq=512 hw=A100
[2026-02-22T14:12:07Z] kv_cache: alloc_page id=0x7f8a3a size=65536 age=0
[2026-02-22T14:56:45Z] kv_cache: mark_page_stale id=0x7f8a3a age=2700 reason=prefetch_prune
[2026-02-22T14:57:03Z] kv_cache: alloc_page id=0x7f8a4c size=65536 age=0
[2026-02-22T15:01:10Z] kv_cache: page_evicted id=0x7f8a3a cause=fragment_coalesce_failure
```

maria.s: "fragment_coalesce_failure" is the interesting bit. we normally compact small free runs into bigger ones. looks like coalesce didn't happen.

alex.k: right — page free list shows many small holes like 8KB/16KB even though page_size is 64KB. I think this is coming from how GQA splits kv pages for multi-head layout on Llama variants. Qwen didn't show this pattern in the same run.

shawn: qwen vs llama difference observed before. Qwen's attention layout produces fewer subpage allocations for MQA because of single tensor packing. Did you run with MQA on/off?

alex.k: this run was MQA off for Llama. interestingly when I enabled MQA the fragmentation reduced but tail latency increased during continuous batching (more frequent small memcpy).

violet: did you check rope scaling math? if rope causes periodic token growth of keys, that can change alignment and lead to uneven subpage usage.

alex.k: good call. I overlaid token-length histogram and rope-scale phase and saw correlation: at multiples of 512 tokens the allocator starts allocating new subpages rather than reusing existing because of different kv-shape.

perf-bot: perf-regression-check: detected 8% P95 increase between commit abc123 and def456 on Llama-2-70b continuous-batch test. likely related to kv allocator change in def456.

maria.s: what's def456? that was the kernel selection heuristic tweak that prefers matmul_opt_v3 for sequences >384 to reduce compute overhead.

shawn: can that kernel change affect memory layout? it shouldn't directly, but it touches execution order and intermediate lifetimes. if kernel_v3 materializes kv slices differently we might get different allocation shapes.

alex.k: I dug into the allocator: when kernel picker uses matmul_opt_v3 we adjust kv-layout to pack heads differently (to favor vectorized matmuls). packing introduces subpage headers => small internal fragmentation.

maria.s: ah, so a perf tweak in compute led to allocator fragmentation that increases memory usage and evictions later. cross-layer coupling.

violet: we should add a lightweight telemetry flag that records "kv_subpage_count" and "coalesce_ops" per request so we can correlate to kernel choice.

alex.k: added a patch locally that emits: kv_subpages=5, coalesce_attempts=2, coalesce_success=0. We need aggregate histos though.

shawn: for immediate mitigation can we bump eviction_threshold to 0.85 or increase page_size to 128KB? tradeoffs: bigger pages reduce fragmentation but increase wasted memory on small contexts.

maria.s: in canary I tried page_size=128KB on Llama and it reduced spike but increased steady state by ~4% — not ideal.

alex.k: another idea: eager defragmentation window during off-peak: run a background sweep that forcibly coalesces small free runs if free_ratio drops below 10%. but sweep is CPU-heavy.

violet: add heuristics: only run defrag if (free_ratio<10% && avg_latency<target*0.9). otherwise risk increasing p99.

perf-bot: note: the job that surfaced this was a 3hr continuous-batch run with steady 150 batch/sec and varying seq length (50-1024).

shawn: action items:
- alex.k: prototype kv telemetry histos + attach to perf traces (ETA 1d)
- maria.s: run canary with page_size=128KB and eviction_threshold=0.85 across Llama/Mistral/Qwen (ETA 2d)
- violet: prototype defrag scheduler with safety conditions (ETA 3d)

alex.k: also tweeting edge-case: MQA on Llama reduces fragmentation but increases memcpy ops that show up as CPU tail spikes. if team cares more about memory footprint we can enable MQA + increase batching window to amortize memcpy cost.

maria.s: for the release notes we should call out: "Fixed: cross-layer regression where kernel picker change increased KV fragmentation on Llama; added telemetry."

shawn: can someone file a perf issue and link to commit refs?

alex.k: created issue #2561 with the traces and attached the canary logs. cc @eng-sre for observation retention.

violet: thanks — adding to the perf board. I think this is a nice example of why kernel selection and memory layout need joint testing. :thumbsup:

maria.s: quick question — any Qwen runs to compare? alex?

alex.k: ran Qwen-2-40b on same workload: no fragmentation spike, but we did see slightly higher eviction churn because Qwen's kv footprint per token is larger (more heads in layout). overall memory remained stable.

shawn: ok let's prioritize Llama fix (telemetry + defrag). also add an integration test that toggles kernel chooser to catch this class of regressions.

alex.k: will put a draft PR up today. thanks all.
_meta: generated for dataset: realistic slack thread about KV cache fragmentation, kernel picker interaction, rope scaling, MQA/GQA differences
